name: Assassination of Rajiv Gandhi, 1991
summary: LTTE suicide bomber Thenmozhi Rajaratnam (Dhanu) killed former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi at an election rally in Sriperumbudur on 21 May 1991. A foreign insurgent group, acting from the Sri Lankan civil war, struck on Indian soil.
scaleRationale: One rally, one night; politically a national rupture. Deaths in the low tens.

resources.note: LTTE fear that Gandhi would send the IPKF back to Sri Lanka

name: Coimbatore serial blasts, 1998
summary: Al-Umma, a domestic Islamist group founded in Coimbatore by S.A. Basha, set off serial bombs on 14 February 1998 as BJP president L.K. Advani arrived for an election meeting. The attacks answered the November 1997 communal killings of Muslims in the same city. Not a transnational franchise.
scaleRationale: One city, one afternoon of bombs, tens dead. Geographically tight; politically statewide.

start.note: Selvaraj murder and the three-day communal outbreak that Al-Umma later cited as motive

end.note: Serial explosions on 14 February; leftover devices recovered over the next days

name: Marad massacres, 2002–03
summary: Communal killing in a Kozhikode fishing hamlet: a two-sided clash in January 2002, then a planned one-sided attack on Hindu fishermen on 2 May 2003. The Thomas P. Joseph Commission blamed local administration, police failure, IUML leaders and Islamist organisers.
scaleRationale: One beach village, two nights, deaths in the low teens. Displacement of hundreds of families.

parties.note: Crime Branch named NDF in the 2003 investigation; a sessions court later convicted dozens of local accused for murder, not a named-org conspiracy charge

sources.title: The Hindu, Marad, where time mended the chasms

killed.note: Five in January 2002 (both communities); eight Hindu fishermen plus one attacker in May 2003. TOI on the Joseph report used 14 across both years.

name: Cauvery riots, 1991 and 2016
summary: Linguistic-ethnic riots in Bengaluru and southern Karnataka over the Cauvery tribunal award. December 1991 saw Tamil neighbourhoods and TN-registered vehicles attacked and thousands flee. Violence returned in September 2016 after a Supreme Court release order.
scaleRationale: A megacity and border towns, two spikes 25 years apart, deaths in the tens, displacement of thousands of Tamil families in 1991.

resources.note: Cauvery sharing between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu

end.note: Violence clustered in December 1991 and September 2016, not continuously

name: Puducherry de facto transfer, 1954
summary: France handed administration of Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam to India on 1 November 1954 after the Kizhoor congress vote. A June coup at Yanam and a Mahe takeover preceded the ceremony. Low violence; colonial integration, not a war.
scaleRationale: Four small enclaves, a negotiated transfer, almost no battle deaths. Political consequence lasted until de jure cession in 1962.

end.note: De facto transfer at Government House, Pondicherry. De jure cession followed on 16 August 1962.

accords.outcome: Administration of the four settlements passed to India on 1 November 1954; sovereignty remained with France until 1962

name: Hyderabad communal riots, 1990
summary: The worst communal killing in Hyderabad after 1948. Advani’s rath yatra and the October 1990 assault on the Babri Masjid raised the temperature; a stabbing in the walled city in December opened weeks of alley-by-alley murder. Not Operation Polo, not the 2007 blasts.
scaleRationale: A historic city, ten weeks of stabbings and arson, deaths in the low hundreds.

resources.note: neighbourhood control in the Old City

parties.note: Army took control of the Old City around 10 December 1990
